name: Female Pelvic Anatomy, Müllerian Duct Anomalies and Pelvic Support

reference.source: Gynaecology by Ten Teachers 21st Edition / Williams Obstetrics 26th Edition
clinicalPearls: Müllerian paramesonephric ducts form fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix and upper vaginal two-thirds
Uterine septum results from failure of midline resorption and carries the highest rate of recurrent pregnancy loss
Cardinal Mackenrodt ligaments carry the uterine artery and provide primary apical suspensory support to the cervix
Ureter passes under the uterine artery water under the bridge approximately 1.5 cm lateral to the cervix
Perineal body serves as the central anchor of the pelvic floor where ten muscular structures converge
reference.pathophysiology: Embryological development of the female reproductive tract depends on paramesonephric Müllerian duct elongation, fusion and canal resorption in the absence of anti-Müllerian hormone. Lateral fusion failures produce bicornuate or didelphic uteri, whereas resorption failure leaves a midline fibrous septum. Pelvic organ support relies on an interconnected network of endopelvic fascia condensations and levator ani muscular tone.
additionalDifferentials: Gartner duct cyst from mesonephric remnant
additionalInvestigations: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging with coronal oblique views
